items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: Ruth was interviewed in Scottsdale, Arizona on March 4, 1995 by Michael Woods.

ctx.x: Versatility might be vocalist Ruth Brown’s middle name. Born in Portsmouth, Virginia in 1928, she first gained public attention when Blanche Calloway brought her to New York in 1949. Since then Ruth has done it all, performing and recording R&B, Gospel and jazz both here and abroad. Her numerous recordings for Atlantic put her on the top of the R&B charts in the 1950s and her versatility allowed her to record with jazz groups such as The Thad Jones- Mel Lewis Orchestra. A recent inductee to the Rock & Roll Hall…
Ruth was interviewed in Scottsdale, Arizona on March 4, 1995 by Michael Woods.

We are filming a jazz archive for Hamilton College, and we are very flattered and privileged to have Ruth Brown, one of the greatest rhythm & blues singers there has ever been, and we want to ask you some questions about your lifestyle and what was going on at the time that you started singing, and some of the other great artists that you’ve worked with, and what all this music means. Tell us in your definition what is rhythm & blues?
